parts.latex:
Shoppers are invited to complete an online survey.

What type of sampling is this?

solutions.latex:
In an online survey that shoppers are invited to complete, each shopper chooses whether to take part. The sample is made up of volunteers.

This is a self-selecting sample.

Hence the answer is A.

parts.latex:
There are 960 students at a high school.

Using stratified sampling, 240 students from the whole school are to be chosen for a survey.

If there are 200 students in Year 12, how many Year 12 students should be chosen?

solutions.latex:
In stratified sampling, each year group is sampled in the same proportion as the whole school.

The sampling fraction is
$$\dfrac{240}{960} = \dfrac{1}{4}$$
So the number of Year 12 students chosen is
$$\dfrac{1}{4} \times 200 = 50$$
So the answer is option C.

parts.latex: A high school has 130 students in each year group from Year 7 to Year 12. A survey is to be conducted to determine the average number of hours studied per week by students at the school. Which of the following would provide the most representative sample for the survey?

solutions.latex:
The year groups are equal in size, and study time is likely to differ between year groups.

A stratified sample takes a proportion from each year group, so every year is represented fairly (for example, the same number of students from each of Years 7 to 12).

A random or systematic sample could miss or under-represent some year groups, and a census would survey every student, which is not a sample.

$$\therefore\ \text{a stratified sample is the most representative}$$

solutions.latex:

$$0.3 \times 250 = 75$$

A group of students were investigating the height of young adult males and females. They went to a local sports stadium and measured the height of the basketball players who were playing that evening.

The statistics included a mean height for young adult males of 192.4 cm and a mean height for young adult females of 186.9 cm.

parts.latex: Is this a biased collection of data? Justify your response.
Suggest one improvement for the survey.

solutions.latex: Yes, this is biased. The data was collected only from basketball players, who are known to be tall, and only those playing that night were measured.
